newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA RAISES MAIN INTEREST RATE TO 300 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA RAISES MAIN INTEREST RATE TO 300 PCT.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) raised its central interest rate to a historic high of 300 percent annually from 108 percent, commercial bank dealers said.
"We received a message from the central bank informing us that a new central interest rate of 300 percent will go into force from September 24," a dealer said.
A central bank official told Reuters that the BNB today sent telex messages to commercial banks to bring their interest rates in line with the new higher central interest rate (CIR).

Despite criticism that the high rate blocks investment in the economy the BNB has raised the CIR several times this year from 34 percent in January in a bid to relieve pressure on the slumping lev on the domestic forex market.

The rate hikes, which were accompanied by tough restrictive measures, however helped briefly stabilise the lev after each rise but could not prevent it from weakening to 237 today from 71 at the beginning of the year.
The BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said recently that the rate could not be reduced until monthly consumer price inflation was curbed to a single-digit figure.
Monthly consumer price inflation was 17.1 percent in August after 23.3 percent in July and 20.3 percent in June.
Cumulative inflation for the first eight months was 113 percent, topping the 1996 government target of 104 percent in the budget revisison passed in July.
Under a recent funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund sealed in July Bulgaria pledged to curb monthly inflation to 2.5 percent at the end of the year.
Local financiers however have long expressed doubts whether the higher rates will restore confidence in local banks plagued by low liquidity.

"With looming bank bankruptcies, soaring inflation and stagnant production one cannot expect rising confidence in either the lev or in the banks," manager of Adlon Discont financial house Andrei Pramov said last month.
Three months ago the central bank sought to have five major banks declared bankrupt in a bid to offset a grave bank crisis.
Lyubomir Filipov told Reuter Financial Television last week that the BNB might seek the closure of more local banks as part of a long delayed financial stabilisation programme.

A BNB board meeting, which began in the morning, was still under way at 1300 local time (1000 GMT) and possible decisions could be expected in the evening, a BNB official said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
